newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican farmers to check crop for sorghum fungus.
newsitem.headline: Mexican farmers to check crop for sorghum fungus.

text.p: Mexico's sorghum farmers have pledged to prevent the spread of ergot fungus on the nation's sorghum crop and test all sorghum for the disease.

An industry conference report obtained by Reuters on Tuesday said farmers committed to emergency measures, such as removing infected plants, monitoring seeds' fertilization, cutting and burning infected regions of the plant and applying fungicide during fertilization.

Sorghum or seed production from infected regions must be officially checked for the fungus before distribution, as part of a national emergency plan, industry leaders said. Other producing areas will also be checked, they added.

The disease was found in Mante, Altamira and San Fernando in Tamaulipas state; Ebano in San Luis Potosi state; San Jose del Valle in Nayarit state; and Panuco in Veracruz state, Gustavo Frias Trevino, director of the National Fitosanitary Reference, said in the report.
"It is unknown if there is a toxic affect on humans," he said.
Meanwhile, industry leaders said the fungus, discovered about two months ago in Mexico, will not have a significant affect on the year's sorghum crop.

"Of a million hectares of sorghum, about five to 10 (hectares) are affected in the northern region, principally in Tamaulipas state," National Agriculture Council vice-president Alvaro Rivera Fernandez told Reuters.

Areas affected were those where harvests had been delayed and weather conditions spurred the fungus' development, he said. The disease infects plants in humid weather with temperatures under 15 degrees celsius when the crop is flowering.
While discounting the overall effect of the fungus in Mexico, Rivera advised against sorghum planting in October, when the scheduled August planting is delayed.
